review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked each declaration for a useful generalisation. I did not open the supplied library sources, so this verdict rests on the file text alone.

The file builds one specific six-vertex graph, so most of its statements are concrete on purpose. Those statements are `rigidSixGraph_adj`, `bfEquiv_one_rigidSixGraph`, `exists_separating_move_rigidSixGraph`, `bfEquiv_two_rigidSixGraph_iff`, `orbitRank_rigidSixGraph` and `internalScottRank_rigidSixGraph`. Each one depends on the concrete adjacency data and is proved by `decide` or `fin_cases`. I found nothing that would generalise without new mathematics.

Two statements already have the generality I would ask for:
- The private lemmas that mention an ordinal are universe-polymorphic in `o`. The one exception is the call inside `rigidSixGraph_iso_eq_refl`, which needs only one fixed universe.
- `two_mem_orbitStable_rigidSixGraph` is stated for tuples of every length `n`.

A possible abstraction is a lemma saying that if level-two back-and-forth equivalence on singletons is equality, then every tuple is orbit-stable at level two. This would only be a single-use refactor, not a useful generalisation.

I also considered restating `rigidSixGraph_iso_eq_refl` as `Subsingleton` or `Unique`. That only changes the form of the conclusion, so I did not report it.
